{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Master Services Agreement — verified playbook review findings

---

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Of the 19 rules assessed, 12 are compliant and 7 are deviations requiring redline. Notably, three deviations are rated critical or otherwise sit in walk-away territory under our playbook, and several of them contradict Customer-favourable provisions found elsewhere in the same document.

The most serious problems are: (i) **no Vendor indemnity at all** — Section 20 contains only a broad one-way Customer indemnity, and Section 9.3 already cross-references infringement remedies in a "Section 20.5" that does not exist; (ii) a **mutual liability cap of one month's Fees applied "without exception"**, which overrides the Excluded Claims definition in Section 21.3 and pulls indemnities, confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap; and (iii) a cluster of restrictive covenants binding us — full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2), a 24-month unlimited-scope post-term non-compete (§ 12.4), and a three-year USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay with "no reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1).

A recurring structural issue is internal inconsistency. Section 12.3 expressly records that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, yet §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 purport to impose exactly those commitments. Similarly, § 11.1 (immediate deletion, no assistance) contradicts the compliant data-return mechanics in §§ 11.2–11.3, and § 2.1 contradicts the convenience-termination right in § 9.4. The Agreement contains no order-of-precedence clause to resolve these conflicts, so the adverse provisions could be read to override the favourable ones. Our redlines therefore remove the adverse provisions rather than relying on the conflict.

On the positive side, the IP package (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4), assignment and change-of-control terms (§ 24, § 9.2), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), audit rights (§ 22), renewal mechanics (§§ 8.2–8.3), governing law and venue (§ 28), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of liquidated damages, MFN and non-solicitation obligations are all compliant — several are better than our preferred position and should be protected in negotiation.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 20 (20.1); cf. § 9.3, § 21.3 |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21.1; cf. §§ 21.2–21.4 |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4; §§ 13.2, 15.1 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 (first of two so numbered); cf. § 12.3 |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4; cf. § 12.3 |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1; cf. §§ 13.2–13.3 |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4; §§ 13.3, 9.2 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4; §§ 27.3, 24.4 |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4; cf. §§ 2.1, 2.2, 9.5 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1; cf. §§ 9.4, 12.3, 7.1 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1; cf. §§ 11.2–11.3 |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2; cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5, 6.1 |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3; §§ 7.1, 8.3 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 |

### Deviation detail and proposed positions

**§ 20.1 — Indemnification (critical).** Section 20 contains only a broad one-way Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way" to our use of the Services; there is no Vendor indemnity anywhere for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. That combination (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services) is walk-away territory, and the fallback is also unmet. Section 9.3 already assumes infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5" that do not exist, confirming the gap. *Proposal:* replace 20.1 with the preferred Vendor indemnity, add usual exclusions and a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, add procure–modify–replace–refund remedies as a new 20.5, and narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.

**§ 21.1 — Limitation of liability (critical).** The cap is mutual but set at Fees actually paid in a single month — far below the fallback of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory (a cap below six months' fees). "Fees" also excludes one-time implementation charges, further shrinking the base, and "without exception" overrides the Excluded Claims definition in 21.3 with no super-cap. Section 21.4's savings language does not cure the quantum. *Proposal:* reset the mutual cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and restore uncapped treatment of Excluded Claims. Sections 21.2 and 21.3 already meet our preferred position and are left intact.

**§ 2.2 — Exclusivity (high).** Binds us to Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit — walk-away territory and a clear failure of the fallback. It also contradicts § 12.3. *Proposal:* make supply non-exclusive and confirm our freedom to source from third parties. *Fallback:* a narrowed 12-month category exclusivity with automatic termination on missed service levels.

**§ 12.4 — Non-compete on Customer (high).** A 24-month post-term restriction covering "any product or service that competes with Vendor" in "any territory", with no carve-out for internal development and an express bar on acquisitions. Walk-away on two counts: post-term duration exceeding 12 months and effectively undefined scope. It directly contradicts § 12.3. *Proposal:* delete § 12.4 and leave § 12.3 to govern. *Fallback:* a single named product, term only, with carve-outs.

**§ 13.1 — Licence grant (high).** Fails the fallback on two material terms: it expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them (walk-away), and it is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 do not cure this — 13.2 reaches only paid-up or embedded software and Vendor Technology, not the Services. *Proposal:* align 13.1 with the model already agreed in 13.2/13.3 — Affiliates and contractors covered, revocation only on material uncured breach after notice and cure, and transfer permitted to an Affiliate or successor.

**§ 2.1 — Take-or-pay commitment (medium).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the walk-away position, and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It contradicts §§ 9.4, 12.3 and 7.1, and with no precedence clause could be read to override them. *Proposal:* replace with pay-for-use language. *Fallback:* a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up.

**§ 11.1 — Transition assistance (medium).** Requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support; as the first-listed provision it contradicts and could override the compliant 30-day machine-readable return and certified deletion in §§ 11.2–11.3. There is no transition period at all, so the clause fails even the 90-day fallback. *Proposal:* replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, with deletion subject to the 11.2/11.3 return and certification mechanics. *Fallback:* 90 days.

**§ 19.2 — Warranty duration (medium).** Sections 19.1, 19.3–19.5 are adequate, but 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformity warranty at 15 days after delivery and then extinguishes any correction or refund obligation — below the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services) and expiring at essentially the same time as the 15-business-day acceptance window in § 6.1, leaving no post-acceptance protection. *Proposal:* extend to 90 days with the § 19.4 remedy preserved for nonconformities reported during the period.

---

## Walk-away items

The following provisions are identified in the findings as sitting in walk-away territory under our playbook. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (§ 20).** Absence of a Vendor IP indemnity combined with a one-way Customer indemnity covering Vendor's own services.
2. **One-month liability cap applied "without exception" (§ 21.1).** A cap below six months' fees, with Excluded Claims overridden and no super-cap.
3. **Full-term exclusivity with no performance exit (§ 2.2).**
4. **24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope (§ 12.4).**
5. **Services licence excluding Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them (§ 13.1).**
6. **Three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1).**
7. **Immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support (§ 11.1).**

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations, prioritising the three critical/walk-away items (§ 20 indemnity, § 21.1 cap, and the § 2.1/§ 2.2/§ 12.4 restrictive-covenant cluster). Each comment will carry the `[Playbook]` prefix, state the position and offer the fallback where one exists.
2. **Flag the broken cross-reference** in § 9.3 to "Section 20.5", which does not exist; our indemnity redline creates that provision and resolves it.
3. **Flag the duplicate numbering** of the two provisions numbered § 2.2 for cleanup.
4. **Propose an order-of-precedence clause.** The Agreement has none, which is what allows §§ 2.1, 2.2, 11.1 and 12.4 to be read against the Customer-favourable §§ 9.4, 11.2–11.3 and 12.3. This is a low-cost structural fix that reinforces our substantive redlines.
5. **Confirm the commercial mandate** on the § 2.1 volume commitment and § 2.2 exclusivity before we concede to either fallback, since both go to deal economics rather than pure legal risk.
6. **Protect the compliant terms** in negotiation — in particular § 9.4 (convenience termination with pro-rata refund and no reciprocal Vendor right), § 24 (assignment and change of control, including § 24.4), §§ 8.2–8.3 (renewal reminder and uplift cap), § 22 (audit limits) and § 18 (insurance) — and resist any trade that erodes them in exchange for movement on the deviations."}
